description:
FILED s536 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-08) from a probe while bisecting the round board's Capture-Tiny movers (not their cause).

REPRODUCER (scratchpad p: ct/d.pl):
    my %d2; sub setit { $_[0] = "via-alias" } setit($d2{k} = "orig"); print "2 $d2{k}\n";
    my @a; sub setx { $_[0] = 9 } setx($a[0] = 1); print "3 $a[0]\n";
  perl 5.40.3: `2 via-alias` / `3 9`.  PCL main (MAIN-READY-76) AND 1191fa1a (MAIN-READY-72): `2 orig` / `3 1` -- pre-existing.

WHY: perl's sassign returns its LEFT operand (the lvalue), so an assignment in an argument slot puts the target itself into @_.  PCL's docs/not-supported.md "@_ argument aliasing -- PARTIAL" lists the shapes that alias (globals, spreads, named-container ELEMENTS, my lexicals for KNOWN writer callees); an ASSIGNMENT whose target is one of those is not among them.  s532c's #4303 made an element assignment an LVALUE for `=~ s///` and `OP=` -- the same fact, one more consumer: the argument slot.

WHERE TO START: the argument lowering that decides "the box already in play is passed through" (ir-spec Â§5.2) -- an assignment node whose target is an aliasing shape should pass the target's box after the store, exactly as #4303 routes `($h{k} = X) =~ s///`.  Capture::Tiny writes `_open $dup{stdin} = IO::Handle->new, "<&=STDIN"` (open on $_[0]) -- it works today only because the stored value is a glob REF (the open reaches the same glob through the copy); a callee that writes $_[0] itself would not.
Bar: guard rows (element, array element, my lexical, our var) perl-probed, fail on base; corpus-diff + wide A/B predicted.
subject: SILENT WRONG: an ASSIGNMENT used as a sub argument is passed as a COPY -- `setit($h{k} = "orig")` / `setx($a[0] = 1)` with `$_[0] = ...` in the callee leaves the element unchanged; perl passes the assignment's lvalue (the element / variable) and $_[0] aliases it
